parsed.headline: Community organizers hold civic engagement fair in Toronto to encourage voter participation

pages.text: Community organizers held a non-partisan fair at the Lawrence Heights Community Centre in Toronto to raise civic engagement and encourage residents to vote in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Organized by the North York Harvest Food Bank, the event included participation from Voice the Vote, a joint initiative by United Way Greater Toronto and Toronto Metropolitan University’s Democratic Engagement Exchange. During the event, Jonathan Dong distributed election handbooks and spoke about the importance of participating in the democratic process. This effort follows previous municipal elections in the city that saw what observers described as a downward trend in voter participation. In the 2023 mayoral byelection won by Olivia Chow, 37 per cent of eligible voters participated, while turnout was less than 30 per cent in the 2022 municipal election and approximately 41 per cent in 2018. Data from the Association of Municipalities of Ontario indicated that across the province, overall voter turnout was nearly 33 per cent in the 2022 municipal elections and roughly 38 per cent in 2018. However, turnout at Toronto's advance polls for the upcoming election was reported as more than 222,000 people, the highest number in more than a decade.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian government declines most Constitutional Review Committee recommendations on natural resources and environment

pages.text: Following the publication of a Government Position Paper regarding the final recommendations of the Constitution Review Committee (CRC), the government of Ghana has declined substantially all proposals concerning lands, natural resources, and environmental thematic areas. The CRC had proposed several reforms, including a clearer public trust framework for natural resources, stronger parliamentary oversight of resource transactions, basic principles for natural resource governance, and improved institutional coordination. Other CRC proposals included the constitutional recognition of ocean governance and the blue economy, the creation of an offence of ecocide, and a guaranteed share of mineral revenue for mining communities. According to MyJoyOnline, the government's position is that existing constitutional provisions are adequate or that these objectives can be achieved through ordinary legislation, such as the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), the Fisheries Act, 2002 (Act 625), the Petroleum Revenue Management Act, 2011 (Act 815), and the Environmental Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1124).

parsed.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth meets Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during unannounced visit

pages.text: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on October 19, 2026, according to a report by Axios citing two sources with knowledge of the matter. Reuters could not immediately confirm the visit, and there was no immediate indication of what was discussed. The Pentagon declined to comment, and Israel’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 19 October 2026 marks a visit occurring ahead of Israel's parliamentary election scheduled for next week, which is the country's first vote since the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023. Opinion polls suggest Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, though the opposition may also struggle to form a government.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh state minister says education reforms must extend beyond curriculum

pages.text: On October 19, 2026, the State Minister for Primary and Mass Education in Bangladesh, Bobby Hajjaj, stated that curriculum reforms alone would not improve primary education unless teacher training, school supervision, infrastructure, and technology are addressed together. Speaking at a dialogue organized by the ministry, the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE), and Unicef, Hajjaj noted that a proposed curriculum would place greater emphasis on English, mathematics, Bangla, digital content, practical activities, and play-based learning. The ministry plans to test teaching materials and assessments in 2027, with a revised curriculum scheduled for introduction in 2028. Additionally, a 12-month practical learning programme has been proposed to cover topics such as child protection, road safety, hygiene, nutrition, digital safety, and environmental protection. A teacher policy is also being prepared to cover recruitment, training, postings, professional development, and evaluation, with Hajjaj stressing that teachers should receive training before entering classrooms. Planning State Minister Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki added that improving the professional skills, status, and salaries of teachers is essential to reducing dropouts and raising education quality.

The ministry presented findings from consultations held between July 26 and September 10 involving more than 3,200 participants across eight divisions. The ministry also proposed common minimum standards for primary schools, including equal instruction time for single- and double-shift schools, with annual teaching hours ranging from 750 for Class I to 900 for Class V, subject to approval. Survey data presented during the dialogue included responses from 1,036 monitoring officials, which found that 86.3 percent could visit no more than 10 schools per month, while 58.2 percent supervised more than 50 schools each. A separate survey of 580 officials found that 84.3 percent wanted duplicate or lengthy reporting requirements reduced. These figures reflect the responses of officials rather than verified inspection records.
